What Clients Tell Us When They Arrive from a Competitor

Two short stories from clients who tried a different company first — or tried on their own — before finding Inquiry Removal. These are the accounts we hear most often.

Story 1 — The Monthly Subscriber Who Ran Out of Patience Kevin D. spent four months enrolled with a generalist credit repair company before he called us. Every month, $99 left his account. Every month, he received an update email that listed “disputes in progress.” Every month, his inquiry count stayed exactly the same. When he finally asked a direct question — are these specific inquiries going to be removed, and when — he was told it “depends on the bureaus.” He came to Inquiry Removal after that conversation. During his free consultation, we identified 27 unauthorized hard inquiries across all three bureaus, explained the specific legal argument that applied to each one, and submitted custom disputes within 24 hours of him signing up. Fifty-five days later, all 27 inquiries were gone. His score had climbed 97 points. The four months he spent with the prior company cost him $396. The work with Inquiry Removal cost $299. The difference wasn’t just financial — it was the experience of working with a company that had a reason to finish the job instead of a reason to keep him enrolled.

“I spent months paying $99 a month and my inquiry count didn’t move. I paid $299 to Inquiry Removal and 27 inquiries were gone in 55 days. I don’t know what the other company was doing but it wasn’t this.”

— Kevin D. | Atlanta, GA ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | 27 Inquiries Removed | +97 Points in 55 Days

Story 2 — The Self-Filer Who Hit a Wall Andre W. from Memphis tried to handle his inquiry disputes himself before he contacted us. He had done his research. He knew about the FCRA. He sent dispute letters to all three bureaus and waited. Equifax came back with “verified.” Experian came back with “verified.” TransUnion deleted two of his inquiries and verified the rest. He didn’t know what to do next — and the forum threads he found online gave him five different answers, none of which worked. He came to us with 18 remaining inquiries, a lot of frustration, and a healthy skepticism about whether anyone could actually fix this. During the consultation, we explained the distinction between a bureau verifying that a pull happened and confirming that it was authorized — a distinction that changes the entire legal argument on a reinvestigation. We built the follow-up disputes from that angle. Within 44 days of signing up, all 18 remaining inquiries were removed. His score moved up 79 points.

“I was skeptical. I thought it sounded too good to be true. I’d already tried on my own and gotten nowhere. Inquiry Removal removed 18 inquiries in 44 days. I don’t know why I waited so long.”

— Andre W. | Memphis, TN ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | 18 Inquiries Removed | +79 Points in 44 Days

When a Competitor Might Actually Be the Better Choice — We’ll Tell You Honestly

This section exists because we believe in giving you complete information, not just the parts that make us look good.

Inquiry Removal is not the right fit if

You need more than inquiry removal. If your credit report has collections, charge-offs, late payments, bankruptcies, or other negative items beyond hard inquiries — Inquiry Removal is not the company for you. We remove hard inquiries exclusively. We are genuinely the best in the country at that one thing, but it is the only thing we do. If your situation requires a broader credit repair strategy, a company like Credit Saint or Lexington Law covers a wider range of negative items. The monthly fee is real and the results are slower, but the scope is broader — and if your needs extend beyond inquiries, that scope matters. You have no unauthorized or excessive hard inquiries. Not every hard inquiry qualifies for removal. Inquiries from credit applications you genuinely authorized — and that were not excessive or improperly obtained — have a much weaker legal argument for dispute. If your free consultation reveals that your inquiries are all legitimately authorized and properly documented, we will tell you that clearly rather than take your money on a case we cannot win. You want an in-person office relationship. We operate entirely online. There is no physical location, no office to visit, and no in-person appointments. If that matters to you, a company with a local presence may be a better fit.

Honest acknowledgment: We know that saying “here’s when you shouldn’t hire us” is not standard marketing practice. We do it because the clients who trust us most are the ones who trusted us enough to hear the full picture first — not a curated version of it.

Where Inquiry Removal Is the Clear Choice — With Specific Proof

If your primary or sole credit issue is unauthorized, excessive, or fraudulent hard inquiries — the comparison is not close. Here is exactly why, with specific evidence for each claim.

We Win on Specialization

Lexington Law, Credit Saint, and The Credit People are generalist companies. Inquiry removal is one dispute type among dozens they handle — treated with the same process they’d apply to a collection or a late payment. We have spent eleven years doing nothing but hard inquiry removal. Every strategy, every letter, every escalation path in our process was developed specifically for inquiry disputes. You cannot replicate that depth with a generalist approach, no matter how large the company is. Proof: 100,437 hard inquiries deleted since 2015. Near-100% success rate. A generalist competitor cannot show you inquiry-specific numbers because they don’t track them separately.

We Win on Cost — By a Significant Margin

The Standard Plan at $299 is a one-time payment. Six months of Lexington Law at their base rate runs $594 to $894 or more — for a service that has no defined endpoint and no flat-fee structure that aligns their incentives with your outcome. Even at the Elite Plan rate of $499, Inquiry Removal costs less than four months of a competitor’s subscription — and when the inquiries are removed, the billing stops completely. Proof: Sophia M. — paid $299, saved an estimated $72,000+ in mortgage interest over 30 years at her improved score. The ROI comparison isn’t theoretical. It’s built into every loan payment she makes.

We Win on Speed

Monthly subscription companies have a structural reason to move slowly — continued enrollment means continued revenue. We have the opposite incentive. Every day your case is unresolved is a day we haven’t delivered what we were paid a flat fee to deliver. We build custom disputes within 24 hours of signup and submit to all three bureaus simultaneously. Most clients see their first removals within 14 to 30 days. Proof: Marcus T. — 19 inquiries removed in 47 days. Diana R. — 34 fraudulent inquiries removed in 61 days. Kevin D. — 27 inquiries removed in 55 days after four unproductive months with a prior company.

We Win on Access

When clients call us, someone answers. When clients have questions, someone responds with a real answer about their specific file — not a scripted update from a rotating case worker who is reading their notes for the first time. Robert Garcia built this company after watching major credit repair companies lose clients to voicemail and automated responses. Direct accessibility is a policy at Inquiry Removal, not a feature listed in a pricing tier. Proof: Maria S. — “Robert picked up the phone every single time I called.” James L. — “I always got a real answer from someone who knew my case.” This is not a marketing claim — it is documented consistently across our 4.9-star Google review profile.

We Win on Alignment

Our incentives and your incentives are the same. You want your inquiries removed as fast as possible. So do we — because our flat fee is already paid and the only way we’ve done our job is if the result is delivered. There is no version of a monthly subscription model where the company’s financial interest and the client’s financial interest are perfectly aligned. There is every version of a flat fee model where they are. Proof: This is structural, not anecdotal. A company that bills monthly earns more money when results take longer. A company that charges a flat fee earns the same amount regardless of speed — which means the only variable it can compete on is how fast it delivers.
